Question 1
?

The population P(t) of owls in a particular forest follows the logistic growth model

dPdt=0.1P−0.0002P2, where t is the time, measured in years. If there were 100 owls in the forest initially, how many owls inhabited the forest after 10 years? Round you answer to the nearest integer.

a
 202
b
 173
c
 289
d
 366
e
 214
Submit

decision.explanation: Write the equation as P'=0.1P(1-P/500). With P(0)=100, the logistic solution is P(t)=500/(1+4e^{-0.1t}). Thus P(10)=500/(1+4e^{-1})≈202.305, which rounds to 202 owls.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
The population $P(t)$ of owls in a particular forest follows the logistic growth model

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=0.1P-0.000\,2{P}^{2},
$$

where $t$ is the time, measured in years. If there were $100$ owls in the forest initially, how many owls inhabited the forest after $10$ years? Round you answer to the nearest integer.
after.worked_solution:
A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=kP(a-P),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>P$ is the carrying capacity. 

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{a}{1+C{e}^{-akt}},
$$

where $C$ is an arbitrary constant.

We start by factoring the given differential equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dP}{dt} & =0.1P-0.000\,2{P}^{2} \\  & =0.000\,2P(500-P)\end{aligned}
$$

From here, we see that the constant of proportionality is $k=0.000\,2,$ and the carrying capacity is $a=500.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
P(t)=\frac{500}{1+C{e}^{-(500\cdot 0.000\,2)t}}=\frac{500}{1+C{e}^{-0.1t}}.
$$

We now substitute the initial condition $P(0)=100$ and solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0) & =100 \\ \frac{500}{1+C{e}^{-0.1(0)}} & =100 \\ 1+C & =5 \\ C & =4\,.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
P(t)=\frac{500}{1+4{e}^{-0.1t}}.
$$

Finally, we substitute $t=10$ into the expression for $P(t),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(10) & =\frac{500}{1+4{e}^{-0.1(10)}} \\  & ≈202.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, after $10$ years, approximately $202$ owls inhabited the forest.

dPdt=kP(a−P),

P(t)=5001+4e−0.1t.

P(10)=5001+4e−0.1(10)≈202.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
The rate of growth in the number of students $P(t)$ in a school who have heard a certain rumor follows the logistic growth model

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=P-0.000\,5{P}^{2},
$$

where $t$ is the time, in hours, since the rumor started spreading. If there were $2$ students who knew the rumor initially, how many students have heard the rumor after $7$ hours?
after.worked_solution:
A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=kP(a-P),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>P$ is the carrying capacity. 

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{a}{1+C{e}^{-akt}},
$$

where $C$ is an arbitrary constant.

We start by factoring the given differential equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dP}{dt} & =P-0.000\,5{P}^{2} \\  & =0.000\,5P(2\,000-P)\end{aligned}
$$

From here, we see that the constant of proportionality is $k=0.000\,5,$ and the carrying capacity is $a=2\,000.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
P(t)=\frac{2\,000}{1+C{e}^{-(2\,000\cdot 0.000\,5)t}}=\frac{2\,000}{1+C{e}^{-t}}.
$$

We now substitute the initial condition $P(0)=2$ and solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0) & =2 \\ \frac{2\,000}{1+C{e}^{-(0)}} & =2 \\ 1+C & =1\,000 \\ C & =999\,.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
P(t)=\frac{2\,000}{1+999{e}^{-t}}.
$$

Finally, we substitute $t=7$ into the expression for $P(t),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(5) & =\frac{2\,000}{1+999{e}^{-7}} \\  & ≈1047.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, after $7$ hours, approximately $1047$ students have heard the rumor.

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is P(t)=a1+Ce−akt, where C is an arbitrary constant.

We start by factoring the given differential equation: dPdt=0.35P−0.0007P2=0.0007P(500−P).

From here, we see that the constant of proportionality is k=0.0007, and the carrying capacity is a=500. Therefore, the general solution is P(t)=5001+Ce−(500⋅0.0007)t=5001+Ce−0.35t.

We now substitute the initial condition P(0)=120 and solve for C. We get 5001+Ce−0.35(0)=1201+C=500120C=256−1=196.

So, we have P(t)=5001+196e−0.35t.

Finally, we substitute t=7 into the expression for P(t), and we get P(7)=5001+196e−0.35(7)≈393.

Therefore, after 7 months, approximately 393 customers were signed up.

content.problem:
The population $P(t)$ of customers signed up for a grocery store’s rewards program follows the logistic growth model

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=0.35P-0.0007{P}^{2},
$$

where $t$ is the time, measured in months. If there were $120$ customers signed up initially, how many customers were signed up after $7$ months? Round your answer to the nearest integer.

After $7$ months, approximately
{{field-1}} customers were signed up.
content.worked_solution:
A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=kP(a-P),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>P$ is the carrying capacity. 

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{a}{1+C{e}^{-akt}},
$$

where $C$ is an arbitrary constant.

We start by factoring the given differential equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dP}{dt} & =0.35P-0.0007{P}^{2} \\  & =0.0007P(500-P).\end{aligned}
$$

From here, we see that the constant of proportionality is $k=0.0007,$ and the carrying capacity is $a=500.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
P(t)=\frac{500}{1+C{e}^{-(500\cdot 0.0007)t}}=\frac{500}{1+C{e}^{-0.35t}}.
$$

We now substitute the initial condition $P(0)=120$ and solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{500}{1+C{e}^{-0.35(0)}} & =120 \\ 1+C & =\frac{500}{120} \\ C & =\frac{25}{6}-1 \\  & =\frac{19}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
P(t)=\frac{500}{1+\frac{19}{6}{e}^{-0.35t}}.
$$

Finally, we substitute $t=7$ into the expression for $P(t),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(7) & =\frac{500}{1+\frac{19}{6}{e}^{-0.35(7)}} \\  & ≈393.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, after $7$ months, approximately $393$ customers were signed up.
